RQ1.primary_observation: BURST p99 latency exceeded NORMAL p99 latency in all 18 conditions with bootstrap 95% intervals above zero.
RQ1.question_focus: Effect of contention/burst conditions on cross-shard latency

RQ2.interpretation_constraint: Associations only; coefficients are not interpreted as causal effects.
RQ2.question_focus: Association of queue-entry contention indicators with subsequent waiting time

RQ3.evidence_location: Chapter 4 CAPC design, scoring function, eligibility rule, atomic locking semantics, aging mechanism and frozen parameters.
RQ3.note: RQ3 is answered through system/algorithm design and implementation verification, not through a standalone inferential experiment.
RQ3.question_focus: Design of an atomicity-preserving contention-aware priority coordination mechanism

RQ4.mixed_model_status: attempted but unusable due singular random-effects covariance; predeclared Wilcoxon fallback used
RQ4.note: No new overall-success criterion was introduced. The frozen preservation implementation evaluates deterministic per-condition/seed constraints and explicitly does not itself declare overall research success.
RQ4.primary_inferential_method: paired Wilcoxon within condition + Holm adjustment

analysis_integrity_notes: CAPC parameters were not retuned after observing primary results.
Diagnostic FIFO is descriptive and excluded from matched atomic causal comparisons.
The primary log-p99 mixed model was attempted but was unusable due to a singular random-effects covariance structure; the predeclared paired Wilcoxon fallback with Holm adjustment was therefore used.
Large transaction-level analyses were performed without sampling using memory-safe streaming or sufficient-statistic implementations while preserving the frozen research definitions.
overall_experimental_status: PRIMARY EXPERIMENT COMPLETE; RQ1, RQ2 AND RQ4 EVIDENCE FROZEN
